deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a derivation. It is a set of aphoristic research-diary notes, continuing the methodological reflections on the previous page (Klein vs. Hilbert, the axiomatic method, 'Axiomschichten'). The only mathematical content is in the first paragraph.

(1) The infinite as the real difficulty. Hilbert contrasts two kinds of statement.
- For a single given number N, the statement 'N is prime' can always be decided by finite computation ('durch Rechnung erzwingen'). Example: trial division by every d with 2 <= d <= sqrt(N).
- The statement 'there are infinitely many primes', in modern form for all n there exists p > n with p prime, cannot be settled by any finite amount of computation ('bis an den jüngsten Tag rechnen'). It needs a 'Gedanke', meaning a proof idea.
- The idea he has in mind is implicitly Euclid's argument (filled in by me). Given primes p_1, ..., p_k, set N = p_1*...*p_k + 1. Then N > 1, and none of the p_i divides N. So any prime factor of N is a new prime.
- In modern terms this proof also gives a computable bound (mine): for every n there is a prime p with n < p <= n! + 1. Bertrand's postulate sharpens this to n < p <= 2n. So each single instance 'there is a prime > n' is again finitely decidable. What no computation can do is establish the universal statement over all n. That is exactly the finite/infinite contrast Hilbert draws.

(2) Where mathematics begins. Mathematics begins as soon as concepts are combined and only what lies in the concepts may be used afterwards. Axioms are singled out ('bes. Axiome'), and they in turn strictly determine the concept: an implicit-definition view. Hence 'wherever pure logic holds, there is already mathematics'. The integer is 'only something special'. He names geometry, mechanics and electron theory as fields open to this treatment, i.e. the axiomatization programme later formulated as his 6th Paris problem.

(3) Methodological maxims:
- 'In der Beschränkung zeigt sich der Meister' (Goethe): less is often more; keep only the essential assumptions and singularities.
- Journals print 'blooming nonsense' beside the deepest truths, and real criticism exists only orally.
- Writing reviews (Referiren) is not only useful but a higher intellectual activity, because it requires overview and understanding of the connections between mathematical topics. The sentence continues on the next page.
errors: No mathematical errors; there are no computations on the page.

Minor logical nuance, not an error: 'infinitely many primes' is a for-all-there-exists statement. Each instance 'there is a prime > n' is in fact finitely decidable, because Euclid's proof bounds the search by n!+1 (or 2n by Bertrand). The non-finitary part is only the universal quantifier over n. Hilbert's informal phrasing is consistent with this.

results.what: Infinitude of primes requires a proof idea, not computation; primality of a given number is decidable by finite computation
results.modern_name: Euclid's theorem; decidability of primality vs. unbounded universal statements (finitary/infinitary distinction)
results.usually_credited_to: Euclid (Elements IX.20); the finitist framing is Hilbert's own, published in the 1920s ('Über das Unendliche', 1925/26)

results.what: Mathematics begins wherever concepts are fixed by axioms and pure logic applies; the integers are only a special case; axiomatize geometry, mechanics, electron theory
results.modern_name: Axiomatic method / implicit definition by axioms; programme of axiomatizing physics (6th Paris problem)
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (Grundlagen der Geometrie 1899; Paris problems 1900; Frege-Hilbert correspondence)

deep.surprise_reason: These are private methodological aphorisms that agree with Hilbert's known views. The infinite as the core difficulty prefigures his 1920s finitism, and the axiomatic method and axiomatizing physics are already in the Paris problems. The early, informal contrast between decidable finite questions and statements about the infinite, and the explicit inclusion of electron theory, are of biographical interest. They are not new results.
